hints.title: Circular Array Duplication Obstacle
hints.text: Circular array wraparound tempts duplicating the full array and scanning repeatedly in quadratic time. How can looping through indices twice with modulo arithmetic resolve circular successors in linear time?

hints.title: Two-Pass Circular Monotonic Invariant
hints.text: Traversing the array twice (length 2 * N) using index % N covers all possible rightward circular paths. Any index popped by a larger element has found its circular next greater element.

hints.title: Two-Pass Modulo Resolution Procedure
hints.text: Initialize res array of size N filled with -1, and an empty index buffer. Loop i from 0 to 2 * N - 1: while the index buffer is non-empty and nums[i % N] > nums[buffer[-1]], pop index j and set res[j] = nums[i % N]. If i < N, push i to the buffer. Return res.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of array nums (1 <= N <= 10^4)
complexity.notes: Two linear passes with index modulo arithmetic; each index pushed and popped at most once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning up to N elements rightward for each element in the circular array takes O(N^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Simulating the doubled circular array virtually via modulo requires only O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Avoiding physical array concatenation and pushing to the stack only during the first pass.
